messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: infer-us-east-1 pool latency spike + node flaps detected (alert: INFER_NODE_FLAP_HIGH)
sara: seeing a flurry of NotReady on 3 nodes in infer-us-east-1, lots of 502s from the inference gateway. anyone oncall? @matthew?
matthew: oncall here, looking. can you paste the node list and recent events?
elaine: pinging infra to see if there's a driver push rolling out in that region, suspected kernel patch last night but not alerted.
ryan: I can take logs. running quick kubectl from jumpbox now.
sara: thanks. output clipped but here's the events and statuses from the controlplane (sanitized):

```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "infer-.*"
infer-us1-node-07   NotReady   2d   v1.25.3   10.0.7.19
infer-us1-node-12   NotReady   3m   v1.25.3   10.0.7.24
infer-us1-node-18   Ready      1d   v1.25.3   10.0.7.31
```

$ kubectl describe node infer-us1-node-07 | egrep -i "kubelet|kernel|oom|nvidia" -A3
Kubelet has restarted 4x in last 10m
Kernel: dmesg contains OOM killer traces for containerd-shim
nvidia: GPU driver lost devices, NVML init error
```
matthew: that matches: kubelet restart + gpu driver resets -> pods getting Evicted/CrashLoopBackOff
matthew: immediate mitigation: cordon the two NotReady nodes (if not already) and scale up infer pool in other AZs, start reroute to west region if capacity allows. we'll also trigger graceful fallback to the smaller-quantized model to reduce memory pressure.
elaine: infra confirms no intentional kernel/driver rollout. looks like a driver upgrade on the cloud image hit a subset of nodes via node auto-repair — investigating.
ryan: running drain on infer-us1-node-07 now, force evict with grace 60s for GPU pods. will watch for evictions failing due to kubelet flapping.

```
$ kubectl cordon infer-us1-node-07
$ kubectl drain infer-us1-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

sara: FYI customer impact: increased tail latencies for some enterprise customers on hosted API; data-ingress shows 3% of requests got 502 during the spike window. I'm drafting an incident notice.
matthew: good. set runbook stage=investigating, severity=high. @deploy-bot can you open a canary reroute to infer-us-west for non-low-latency customers?
deploy-bot: Canary reroute config applied: 15% traffic to infer-us-west, 85% to primary. watch for model perf regressions.

elaine: infra found kernel log entries on node-07 that look like:
```
[  123.456789] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (python) total-vm: 1423456kB, anon-rss: 1200000kB
[  123.460000] oom_reaper: reaped process 12345
[  125.000000] device 0000:65:00.0: GPU lost, hw reset failed
```
elaine: NVML reports device lost before kubelet restart. likely CUDA or driver crash triggering container OOMs.

ryan: nvidia-smi on node-18 (still Ready) shows GPUs healthy. suspect a bad batch of nodes with corrupted driver state. I'm adding a taint we can use to keep scheduler from reusing suspect nodes until patched.
matthew: do it. also kick off node replacement via autoscaler for those NotReady nodes.

```
$ kubectl taint nodes infer-us1-node-07 node-role.kubernetes.io/suspect=true:NoSchedule
$ asg replace-instance --instance-id i-0abc123 --force
```

sara: coordinating customer comms: incident page draft — we'll note degraded throughput in infer-us-east-1, mitigation: traffic reroute & model fallback, ETA for full restore ~30-45m pending node replacement.
matthew: handoff if I'm paged again in next 20m to @elaine. I'm going to continue monitoring scaling & evictions.

elaine: infra says image rollout flagged a bad kernel/driver combo on 6 nodes. they're pausing image pipeline and rolling a hotfix. they'll reprovision the affected nodes once healthy image is ready. ETA 40m.
ryan: observed one GPU pod failback log with CUDA error:

```
E cuda: failed to allocate 1099511627776 bytes: out of memory
E runtime: failed to restore kv-cache
```

ryan: that large allocation looks like runaway mem growth in a serving workload — we should also set a per-pod memory limit stricter to fail faster on bad models.
matthew: agreed. open a quick PR to set memLimit=14Gi for gpu-serving in the pool, but only apply to the autoscaled replacement nodes to avoid mass restarts.
sara: do we have capacity to take more traffic west if replacements slow? metrics show 60% headroom in us-west and europe clusters.
matthew: yes. i'll increase canary to 35% now and set automatic increase if 5xxs drop.

```
deploy-bot: Canary update: 35% -> infer-us-west. Auto-scale policy: enabled.
```

elaine: infra hotfix image is ready, rolling to a single node for validation. will monitor NVML stability and kubelet uptime.
ryan: validation pass on one reprovisioned node. NVML shows stable GPUs for 15m, kubelet not crashing. starting phased replace of the remaining 2 nodes.

sara: customer comms sent: "We've mitigated a regional GPU host instability in us-east-1 by diverting traffic and replacing affected nodes. Some customers experienced 502s and elevated tail latency for ~20 minutes. We're continuing validation before returning traffic."
matthew: good. i'm marking incident: mitigation-in-place. keeping thread open for final restore.

(25m later)
matthew: all replaced nodes show Ready, kubelet uptime > 20m, no NVML errors. scaling back canary to normal 0% to us-west. rolling rollback of memLimit PR if it caused regressions.

```
kubectl uncordon infer-us1-node-07
kubectl untaint nodes --all node-role.kubernetes.io/suspect-
```

sara: final telemetry: 5xxs back to baseline, tokenized throughput normal. postmortem owners: matthew (eng-oncall) + elaine (infra). I'll open incident ticket and add logs.
elaine: root cause hypothesis: GPU driver instability on a subset of nodes combined with high-memory serving requests leading to kernel OOM and kubelet restarts. remediation: pin image without bad driver, stricter per-pod memory limits, autoscaler replacement heuristics, and improved NVML healthchecks in node-exporter.
ryan: adding a short-term alert for NVML device resets to catch this earlier.

matthew: thanks all. handoff to ops for followups. going to sleep :coffee: anyone else with followups ping me in the incident ticket.
